messages:
matt_r: Quick sync — thinking of replacing current SM capability probe with a lightweight runtime capability handshake. goal: avoid expensive microbench on cold start but still pick optimal attention / kernel path for A100 / H100 / L4.
chloe: +1 to avoiding long probes. did a short perf sweep yesterday — a 5-iteration microbench was enough to separate tiling choices on L4 but inconclusive on H100 when mixed fp8/fp16.
raj: curious about safety: if handshake claims features but kernel later faults (rare), do we fallback automatically? we need a clear rollback path in runtime.
lina: proposal: two-phase approach — 1) capability handshake that enumerates supported SM ops + driver-reported features, 2) fast correctness smoke test for the selected kernel (cheap, <5ms) before serving traffic.
matt_r: that sounds good. handshake should read driver capability registers + cudaGetDeviceAttribute where possible, then produce a feature vector: e.g. [tensor_ops_v2, async_copy, shfl_sync, fp8_accel].
chloe: microbench snippets I used (pseudo):
```
// 3 small kernels, <2ms each
launch(attn_tile_64); // measure single-step throughput
launch(kv_memcpy_async);
launch(tensor_core_mma_fp8);
```
if tensor_core test times out or high error -> mark fp8 as unstable.
raj: ok but we must persist results per-instance and attach a TTL; driver updates / firmware can change behavior mid-run. TTL maybe 1h and recheck during low traffic.
lina: agree. also suggest scoring heuristic for path selection instead of binary gate. e.g. score = perf_estimate - safety_penalty. then choose path with highest score above threshold.
matt_r: good point. scoring lets us prefer safer fp16 path on H100 when fp8 wins only marginally.
chloe: note: L4 shows weird memory-alignment sensitivity with KV cache for tile=128. our runtime should have an alignment-normalizer rather than relying on kernel fallback.
raj: interface boundary question — should handshake and scoring live inside serving runtime or in the orchestration layer? my vote: runtime owns immediate checks; orchestration can suggest policy (e.g., prefer cost-saving kernels for batch jobs).
matt_r: agree. runtime for immediate correctness/perf; control plane to push policy and collect telemetry.
ci-bot: test-run 1769876543-heatmap finished: attn_tile_64 -> 12.3ms, attn_tile_128 -> 11.9ms (L4) — variance 7%.
chloe: thanks CI data. variance means we should be conservative on L4 for tile=128 unless memory alignment ensured.
infra-bot: FYI deployed runtime change in staging that exposes /runtime/capabilities and /runtime/score for inspection.
lina: two follow-ups: (1) add explicit fallback path mapping in config (pattern -> [preferred, fallback1, fallback2]) (2) log handshake + smoke test results to console at WARN level when mismatch occurs.
matt_r: I'll draft small RFC describing handshake proto, score formula, TTLs, and smoke-test corpus. aim to land RFC by EOD Friday. any objections?
raj: no objections. request: include a section on observability for intermittent false positives (e.g., FP8 passes then fails under load).
chloe: also include a short list of kernels we want to keep hot-path (attn_tile_64/96/128, kv_async, kv_prefetch) and rules for when to JIT-disable a kernel.
matt_r: noted. thanks all. I'll post RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
